item.title: Israel deports hundreds of Gaza flotilla activists after international backlash
item.description: The Israeli government on Thursday released and deported hundreds of flotilla activists who attempted to breach Israel's naval blockade of Gaza. Outrage abroad over the activists' treatment prompted several countries to summon Israeli envoys to hear their concerns. About 420 activists departed Israel on planes bound for Turkey, where they landed Thursday evening in Istanbul. item.title: Death toll from Israeli strikes on Lebanon passes 3,000, officials say
item.description: It marks a grim milestone in the conflict between Israel and the Lebanese armed group Hezbollah since March, despite a nominal ceasefire.

item.title: Hezbollah support endures in south Lebanon as ceasefire fails to stop war with Israel
item.description: Despite continuing Israeli attacks and occupation, many people in the south still believe the armed group is the only force capable of defending them.

item.title: Israeli Minister Threatens to Evict Palestinians From West Bank Hamlet
item.description: Bezalel Smotrich, the hard-line minister, said he was retaliating for the International Criminal Court prosecutor seeking his arrest, something the court did not confirm nor deny.

item.title: Early War Goal Was to Install Hard-Line Former President as Iran’s Leader
item.description: An Israeli strike designed to free Mahmoud Ahmadinejad from house arrest in Tehran, U.S. officials said, was part of an effort to bring about regime change and put him in power.

item.title: Israel's Ben-Gvir sees 'no innocent people in Gaza or even Europe': Journalist Gideon Levy
item.description: FRANCE 24's François Picard welcomes veteran Israeli journalist and Haaretz columnist Gideon Levy. He offers a scathing analysis of Israeli politics, the Gaza war, the unprecedented rise of xenophobic nationalism and Israel's growing dependence on the United States. Speaking from Tel Aviv amid mounting electoral tensions, Levy argues that "everything – war and peace, domestic politics, legislation – is now covered by the shadow of the upcoming elections".

item.title: Mamdani won't attend Israel Day Parade, breaking decades-long mayoral tradition amid antisemitism surge
item.description: NYC's Israel Day Parade expects record turnout after Mayor Mamdani confirmed he will not attend, drawing criticism from Jewish leaders citywide.

item.title: Video Shows Itamar Ben-Gvir Taunting Pro-Palestinian Activists
item.description: The national security minister, Itamar Ben-Gvir, posted a video in which he is seen with handcuffed activists forced to kneel on the deck of a ship. It drew a rebuke from Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

item.title: Middle East live: US military at ‘peak readiness’, CENTCOM says, as Pakistan mediates Iran talks
item.description: The US Central Command (CENTCOM), which oversees military operations in the Middle East, on Thursday said the USS Abraham Lincoln is maintaining “peak readiness” in the region. It came as Pakistan stepped up diplomatic efforts to get US-Iran peace talks on track. Follow our liveblog for the latest developments.

item.title: Turkey political crisis simmers as opposition vows to resist court ruling
item.description: Turkey's political ​opposition dug in on Friday to resist an unprecedented court ruling that ousted its leader and annulled its congress, inflaming a political crisis that critics say aims to further prolong President Tayyip Erdogan's 23-year rule. The CHP condemned the ruling as a "judicial coup" and Ozel vowed to fight it through legal appeals and to personally remain "day and ‌night" in the main opposition party's headquarters in Ankara.
